plan: Since this is a single round with no history, I must maximize profit by balancing the bid against my value of $10. Bidding too high risks overpaying if I win, while bidding too low risks losing the auction. To maximize profit, I will bid slightly below my value, say $9.9, as it ensures I do not overpay and still have a chance to win if others undervalue their bids. This approach minimizes potential loss while maximizing profit potential if I win.

To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the average expected bid of the others. With no history, assume others bid around their value. My value is $30, so bidding slightly above, like $30.1, increases my chance to win and ensures profit if I do. This strategy minimizes loss in the worst-case scenario of overbidding.

Given my value of $25, I aim to bid below this to ensure profit if I win. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the midpoint between $0 and $25, considering others may bid close to their value. A bid of $15 allows for a potential win while minimizing loss risk. This strategy balances the chance of winning against the risk of overpaying. I must avoid bidding too close to $25 to ensure a positive outcome.
